T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it. ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/overview.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

# ARTEX **Autonomous penetration testing that keeps its receipts.** (upstream: [Autumn-27/ARTEX](https://github.com/Autumn-27), AGPL-3.0) Self-hosted multi-agent offensive security. A planner explores, workers run real tools, and every finding stays bound to the assets and HTTP traffic that prove it. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/BaaRai/ARTEX?label=release&color=6b34db)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](LICENSE) [![CI](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Go](https://img.shields.io/github/go-mod/go-version/BaaRai/ARTEX?color=6b34db)](go.mod) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Install](#installation) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [Security](SECURITY.md)
--- ARTEX is a self-hosted, LLM-driven penetration testing platform. It is not a chat wrapper around a scanner: a planner splits a goal into intents, workers execute them with real tools, and the results are written back into **two linked graphs**: one for what you know about the target, one for how the test is progressing. Every finding can carry the captured request and response that justify it, and every autonomous action passes through scope rules, approval gates and budgets. - **It explores, it doesn't chat.** Goal decomposition, intent dispatch, worker execution and write-back form a closed loop that keeps advancing until the goal is proven. - **Two graphs, one audit trail.** The shared asset graph says *what exists*; the per-task exploration graph says *what was tried, what it produced, and why*. Anchors link the two. - **Findings with evidence.** A recording MITM proxy and a browser extension capture real traffic; findings, evidence quotes and retests are tied to the exact request/response. - **Autonomy with brakes.** Human-in-the-loop approvals, argv-prefix rules, scope/deny gates, token and turn budgets, a target noise governor, and prompt-injection framing on tool output. - **Self-hosted and model-agnostic.** One Go binary with the Next.js UI embedded, PostgreSQL, your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local Ollama. --- ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and optionally an LLM key) docker compose up -d --build # builds from this checkout, starts PostgreSQL ``` Open **http://localhost:8787**. On the first visit `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup: ```bash docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token" ``` > There is no prebuilt Docker image to pull: the image is always built from your checkout. > For all installation paths (script, binaries, source, release archives), see [Installation](#installation). --- ## Multi-provider workers In **System → LLM**, configure the profiles you want to use. In **System → Settings**, set the concurrent worker count to at least **2** before starting a task (the count applies to subsequently started tasks). In **System → Agents → Worker**, leave the model set to follow the task; a fixed Worker model takes precedence over rotation. When creating a task, select both profiles in **LLM config chain**, arrange their order, and enable **Enable multi-LLM worker rotation**. For an existing task, open its LLM config control, change the switch or profile order, and save. Rotation assigns successive worker intents A, B, A, B, regardless of completion order. Separate intents can run concurrently on different providers; each intent keeps its selected provider unless it fails over. Planner and other unbound roles continue using the task's current profile. Turning rotation off restores ordered task-level failover. An excluded provider is skipped, so an intent pinned to an exhausted profile falls back to the task's current profile instead of retrying it; rotation keeps cycling the whole list and does not rebalance around a dead provider. Saving the chain resets their failure state. Changes do not interrupt in-flight calls. The rotation cursor starts again after a server restart and saving the chain does not reset it; the profile order and switch remain persisted. The task creation and `PUT /api/tasks/{id}/llm` APIs accept `llm_rotate: true` alongside the ordered `llm_profile_ids`. Omitting `llm_rotate` on an update preserves its value. ## Screenshots | Tasks | Findings | | :---: | :---: | | ![Tasks](screenshots/tasks.png) | ![Findings](screenshots/findings.png) | | Task execution: sessions and tool calls | Exploration graph | | :---: | :---: | | ![Execution](screenshots/sessions.png) | ![Exploration graph](screenshots/graph.png) | | Asset coverage graph | Traffic recording | | :---: | :---: | | ![Asset coverage graph](screenshots/assets_test.png) | ![Traffic](screenshots/traffic.png) | | Human-in-the-loop chat | Interception approvals | | :---: | :---: | | ![Chat](screenshots/chat.png) | ![Interception](screenshots/intercept.png) |
More screenshots (assets, agents, LLM, logs) | Assets | Agent management | | :---: | :---: | | ![Assets](screenshots/assets.png) | ![Agent](screenshots/agents.png) | | LLM configuration | Backend logs | | :---: | :---: | | ![LLM](screenshots/llm.png) | ![Logs](screenshots/logs.png) |
--- ## How it works ### Dual-graph architecture: exploration graph + asset graph ARTEX separates *what the goals are* from *how far testing has progressed* into two independent graphs linked by anchors: - **Asset graph (shared across tasks).** One source of truth for `root_domain / subdomain / ip / service / app / endpoint`, owned by companies. Parent-child relationships and deduplication keys are computed by the program; agents only submit raw observations. - **Exploration graph (per task).** The task's reasoning and progress: `goal / intent / fact / finding / hint` nodes connected by `spawns / derived_from / yields / proves` edges into a lineage chain. - **Anchors link them.** `exploration_anchors(node_id, asset_id)` ties intents, facts and findings to concrete assets: which assets a direction touched, and which intents tested a given asset. This also powers **asset test coverage** and the coverage graph. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph EG["Exploration graph (per-task · advance chain)"] direction TB G["goal"] I1["intent A"] F1["fact"] I2["intent B"] FD["finding (vulnerability)"] G -->|spawns| I1 I1 -->|yields| F1 F1 -->|derived_from| I2 I2 -->|proves| FD end subgraph AG["Asset graph (globally shared · source of truth)"] direction TB RD["root_domain"] SD["subdomain"] SV["service"] EP["endpoint"] RD --> SD --> SV --> EP end I1 -. anchor .-> SD F1 -. anchor .-> SV I2 -. anchor .-> EP FD -. anchor .-> EP ``` The **planner** reads the exploration graph, judges goals, and dispatches intents only when there is an uncovered direction; a **worker** claims one intent, executes it, writes assets/facts/findings back into both graphs, then stops. ### The engine loop The engine is event-driven: any graph change wakes the planner, workers claim and execute intents, write-back triggers the next round, until `prove_goal` closes the task. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant EV as graph-change debounce participant P as planner participant FR as frontier intent queue participant W as worker participant PX as recording proxy participant DB as dual graphs + activity EV-->>P: wake up P->>DB: read situation (graph_overview prefetch + coverage/scope) P->>FR: dispatch 0..N intents (with asset_ids) Note over P,FR: most wake-ups dispatch 0 (no new direction means done) W->>FR: claimNext claims one intent W->>DB: fetch the raw assets of the intent's asset_ids W->>PX: real tool execution (Kali / Bash / HTTP) PX-->>W: response (fully traced + CA verified) W->>DB: write back fact / asset / finding + per-step activity DB-->>EV: graph change EV-->>P: wake again (closed loop) ``` ### Durable attack chains, shared worker memory Real attack chains are multi-step and ordered (find an injection → get credentials → move laterally). The planner keeps a **todolist retained per task across wake-ups**: it records the chain once, then dispatches the next step only when its prerequisites are satisfied by facts. Workers can also **search each other's execution traces** (`search_all_worker_traces`, `list_worker_traces`, `get_worker_trace`). Observations that never became formal facts (an error message, a response snippet, a hidden parameter) are still reusable by the next worker, while each worker remains confined to the intent it claimed. --- ## Features ### Evidence, not chat logs - **Recording MITM proxy** (`:8788`) with a generated CA: every Bash/HTTP tool call is traced, and request/response evidence can be bound to a finding. - **Browser extension** (`extension/`) for authenticated targets: log in once (captcha, email OTP, 2FA included), capture the session, and the requests/responses land in the same traffic store.
Using the traffic capture extension - Load the unpacked extension from `extension/` (Chrome/Edge: Developer Mode → Load unpacked); - In the popup, set your ARTEX URL and token, then press **Start capture** on the tab you are browsing; - Use the site normally; text requests/responses are batched to `POST /api/traffic/ingest` (authenticated). Binary bodies (images, fonts) are skipped, bodies are truncated at 256 KiB, batches are capped at 50 entries; - Press **Stop** when done. Everything stays in your local traffic store.
- **Verified findings**: findings carry a POE level, a verification status and a note; a finding is `verified` only when a bound proof/response and verbatim evidence quotes support it. Gzip/deflate bodies are decoded before the quote check. The findings table supports bulk status updates, and the report and export show each finding's proof strength next to its status. - **Traffic replay**: open a captured exchange and replay the recorded request (method, URL, headers and stored body) from the traffic detail; replay stays disabled while only the body preview is loaded. - **Vulnerability retest loop**: a dedicated `retester` agent re-runs a finding with optional fixed version/conditions, records `Still reproducible / Fixed / Cannot confirm`, and can move the finding to `Fixed` automatically. Original evidence and reports are preserved. - **Reports and exports**: findings, evidence and task archives, with traffic snapshots kept encrypted at rest. ### Control without slowing down - **Interception gate**: every tool call can require human approval, with rules by `string`, `regex` or **argv prefix**. An argv rule is a JSON array of 1 to 8 tokens (Bash only, for example `["git","push"]`); it matches only a single simple command whose parsed prefix equals the pattern exactly. Pipes, lists, redirections, prefix assignments, subshells, background jobs, wrapper programs and command/parameter substitutions do not match; flags are ignored by construction (`["git","push"]` covers `git push --force`, but `git -C /repo push` matches nothing). Each approval records who decided: `human`, `rule`, `model` or `system`. - **Scope and target gate**: scope rows define the coverage denominator; assets outside the declared scope are not explored. The target gate (off by default, API-only) can refuse destinations that were not approved. - **Budgets**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a whole task (planner and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Near the limit the task enters a forced wrap-up; a worker is not started when the remaining budget cannot cover it. Spend already in `llm_usage` is restored after a restart. A task that is already inside the wrap-up reserve only has that reserve left, so the revived run wraps up instead of starting another worker. The per-worker cost estimate starts again from the defaults (50,000 tokens and 10 turns) until a worker finishes in this process. - **Noise governor**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE=quiet|balanced|aggressive` paces requests ARTEX sends to targets (per-host rate, burst, in-flight limit, jitter, backoff on 429/503, short GET caching). With a profile set, agents also receive low-and-slow flags for the installed scanners. - **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Disable with `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0`. ### Assets and coverage - **Coverage ledger and force-directed coverage graph**: in-scope assets are highlighted as tested or untested, with linked intents, facts and findings per node. - **Company-scoped asset graph**: shared across tasks, deduplicated by the program, with domain → subdomain → service → endpoint containment. - **ScopeSentry sync**: pull asset data from a [ScopeSentry](https://github.com/Autumn-27/ScopeSentry) instance by project or task, merged by company scope into the asset graph for agents to explore.
Syncing from ScopeSentry - On the **Asset Sync** page, enter the ScopeSentry address and API key; - Choose the targets and asset types by **project** or **task** (domains / subdomains / IPs / ports / sites / endpoints…); - Import: rows are merged by company asset scope and become part of the asset graph.
- **Task categories, templates, relations and archives** for repeatable engagements. ### Platform - **LLM profiles with failover**: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible relays and keyless Ollama; multiple profiles per task with automatic failover. - **Token accounting**: per-task and per-session usage, cache reads/writes, and an LLM record view for every call. - **MCP servers, skills, memory and a workspace**: extend the agent with remote tools and reusable prompt/playbook material. - **Web search**: the agent's search tool uses Brave, Tavily or the opt-in Keenable backend, configured in **System → Settings** with the key encrypted at rest; search can also egress through its own proxy. - **Single binary**: the Next.js UI is embedded with `go:embed`; PostgreSQL is the only external dependency. --- ## Installation > Requires **PostgreSQL**; exploration requires an **LLM** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or > `OPENAI_API_KEY`, also configurable in the UI). ### Option 1: one-click install script (recommended) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX ./install.sh ``` The script detects or installs Docker, then offers **① all-Docker** (writes `.env`, runs `docker compose up -d --build`) or **② local build and run** (generates `config.json`, builds the embedded binary, starts it). Open **http://localhost:8787**; `/setup` asks for the one-time setup token printed at startup (`docker compose logs artex | grep "Setup token"`). The UI listens on `127.0.0.1` by default. To reach it from another machine (or from Windows when ARTEX runs inside WSL), set `ARTEX_BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0` in `.env` (the setup token still protects the first-run claim), or keep loopback and use a reverse proxy or SSH tunnel. ### Option 2: Docker Compose (manual) ```bash git clone https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX.git cd ARTEX cp .env.example .env # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD, optionally ANTHROPIC_API_KEY docker compose up -d --build # → http://localhost:8787 ``` The image includes a scanner toolchain (`nmap`, `nuclei`, `httpx`, `katana`, `ffuf`, `dalfox`, `sqlmap`, `ripgrep`, `curl`, `npm`, …); `./skills` and `./data` are persisted via bind mounts. For remote MCP you can choose `http` (Streamable HTTP) or `sse` (legacy SSE) in system settings. Legacy SSE servers usually establish the event stream with `GET /sse` and receive JSON-RPC over `/message?sessionId=...`; configure the URL as `/sse` and send `Authorization: Bearer `. ### Option 3: prebuilt binaries (Releases) Download the zip for your platform from [Releases](https://github.com/BaaRai/ARTEX/releases). It contains `artex`, `start.sh` (`start.bat` on Windows), `skills/` and `config.example.json`: ```bash cp config.example.json config.json # fill in the database connection ./start.sh # → http://localhost:8787 ``` Start with `start.sh` / `start.bat`, not `./artex`: it is a daemon script that restarts the process after a backoff. To keep it in the background: `nohup ./start.sh >artex.log 2>&1 &`. #### Verifying a release Each release attaches `SHA256SUMS` and a CycloneDX SBOM, `artex-.cdx.json` (Go modules in the linux/amd64 binary, the frontend `package-lock.json`, `go.mod`/`go.sum`), next to the zips. The zips also carry a GitHub build provenance attestation. Releases published before this was added have neither. ```bash sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # add --ignore-missing if you downloaded only some zips gh attestation verify --repo BaaRai/ARTEX # built by this repository's release workflow ``` ### Option 4: build the single binary from source ```bash cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex ./start.sh ``` Only `-tags embedui` embeds the frontend into the binary. ### Option 5: cross-platform release archives `build.sh` builds and embeds the frontend, strips debug info, and writes zips for Linux amd64/arm64, macOS amd64/arm64 and Windows amd64 by default: ```bash ./build.sh --release # output: dist/artex--*.zip ARTEX_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release ./build.sh --target linux/amd64 --upx ``` UPX is disabled by default: self-extracting binaries may be incompatible with some kernels, virtualization environments or security policies. Pass `--upx` only after confirming the target runtime supports it. --- ## Configuration **Database** (`config.json`, or the `ARTEX_PG_DSN` environment variable): ```json { "database": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 5432, "user": "artex", "password": "yourpass", "dbname": "artex", "sslmode": "disable" } } ``` **LLM**: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...` (or `OPENAI_API_KEY`), or configure it in the UI's "LLM Configuration" page, which can also add a local Ollama server as a keyless provider (format "Ollama", default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`). Optional: `ARTEX_LLM_PROVIDER` (`anthropic | openai | openai-responses | ollama`), `ARTEX_LLM_MODEL`, `ARTEX_LLM_BASE_URL`, `ARTEX_LLM_PROXY`. **Base URL gotcha**: for the Anthropic format, enter the host **without** `/v1` (for example `https://api.anthropic.com`); ARTEX appends `/v1/messages`. OpenAI-format providers append `/chat/completions` (or `/responses` for `openai-responses`), so their base **does** end in `/v1` (for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`). **OpenAI-compatible gateways**: any provider that serves an OpenAI-style `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint works through the **OpenAI** format — no dedicated format needed. Create a profile with format **OpenAI**, set **Base URL** to the gateway's `/v1` root, paste the key, then click the **↻** button next to *Model* to load the provider's catalog (`GET /v1/models`) and pick a model; models the provider adds later appear on the next refresh. For example, [NotHoly](https://notholy.com) (offensive-security models) uses base URL `https://api.notholy.com/v1` with an API key from its console. **Task archive storage**: local disk by default. Set `ARTEX_ARCHIVE_STORAGE=s3` to store cold task packages in an S3-compatible bucket and release their local package space after verification. Existing local archives remain usable. See [Task archive storage](docs/task-archive-storage.md) for configuration, permissions, integrity checks, temporary disk requirements and recovery. **Concurrency**: work agents per task, in "System Settings" (default 3). **Untrusted-output boundary (on by default)**: tool results for the worker, planner, chat and main agent are framed between nonce-tagged markers so the model treats them as data, not instructions. Unset or empty, the boundary is on; set `ARTEX_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0` (or `false` / `off` / `no`) to disable it. Cost: about 154 bytes per tool result plus one system note. **Noise profile (off by default)**: `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE` paces the requests ARTEX sends to targets (WebFetch, HTTP custom tools, the enrich probe). Unset or `off` keeps today's behaviour: no limit, no cache. `quiet` = 2 req/s per host (burst 4, 1 in flight), `balanced` = 5 req/s (burst 10, 2 in flight), `aggressive` = 20 req/s (burst 40, 4 in flight). A profile adds jitter, backs off on 429/503 (honours `Retry-After`, bounded retries, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), deduplicates identical in-flight GETs and caches them briefly (60/30/10 s; never POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), and logs a per-host noise line each minute. `ARTEX_TARGET_USER_AGENT` sets a User-Agent on target requests that carry none. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests) are paced too, per host by the same rate and jitter, and counted in the same per-host lines. The in-flight caps, retries and cache apply only to ARTEX's own requests. This is best effort, not a security boundary. Raw scanners such as nmap are not paced, and neither is a command that bypasses the proxy (`--noproxy`, a removed proxy variable). With capture off, nothing launched from Bash is paced. The low-and-slow prompt block supplies the rate flags in every case. The **Target noise** card in System settings sets the profile at runtime (no restart) and shows the per-host counters; once saved, that setting takes precedence over `ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE`. **Low-and-slow agent guidance (off by default)**: when a noise profile is set, the planner, worker, main agent and chat agents receive a code-owned prompt block with the profile's per-host limits and exact rate/delay flags for the installed scanners. It tells them to test one host at a time, back off on 429/503 and never raise the rate to meet a deadline. **Run budgets (off by default)**: `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_TASK_BUDGET_TURNS` cap a task's total spend (planner rounds and workers); `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TOKENS` / `ARTEX_INTENT_BUDGET_TURNS` cap one worker run. Unset or `0` means unlimited. A worker is not started when the remaining task budget cannot cover its estimated cost (the average of finished workers, else 50,000 tokens and 10 turns). Near the wrap-up reserve (the larger of 5% and 20,000 tokens, and 2 turns) the task enters a forced wrap-up: the planner writes a summary and final goal judgment, and workers may only write back. The task then ends `done` if its goals are met, else `timeout`. Practical floor: below 50,000 tokens no worker starts; 50,000-70,000 typically gives one worker then wrap-up; pick well above 70,000 for real exploration. Planner, worker, judge, and compactor rows in `llm_usage` are counted back into the cap when a ledger is created, including after a restart and after a revived run drops its ledger. A restored task already inside the wrap-up reserve does not get another worker: only that reserve remains, and the run wraps up. Chat, goal decomposition, and side questions are stored on the same task and are not counted. The per-worker average is not restored (usage rows have no run boundary), so the estimate starts from the defaults until a worker finishes in this process. **Common flags**: `./start.sh -addr :8787 -proxy :8788` (`-addr` frontend/API, `-proxy` traffic recording proxy). ### Reverse proxy deployment (HTTPS / exposing only 443) The frontend, API and SSE stream share port 8787 (the binary listens on `127.0.0.1:8787` by default; the Docker container publishes on `127.0.0.1`), and the activity stream is same-origin by default, so **no `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` is needed**: expose 443 and keep 8787 internal. SSE keeps a long-lived connection with continuous pushes, so the proxy **must disable buffering**; otherwise the browser connects but never receives events. Nginx example: ```nginx server { listen 443 ssl; server_name your.domain.com; # ssl_certificate / ssl_certificate_key ... location / { # 512 MiB combined file limit plus 1 MiB of multipart metadata. client_max_body_size 513m; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; # SSE essentials: buffering off, long timeouts, HTTP/1.1 proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; } } ``` **Login rate limit behind a proxy**: login allows 10 attempts per minute per client IP. Behind a proxy every request comes from the proxy's address, so without further setup all users share one budget and an attacker who fails 10 logins blocks everyone, admin included, for up to 15 minutes. Keep the `X-Forwarded-For` line and set `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (comma-separated CIDRs, empty by default) to the address ARTEX sees the proxy connect from: - **nginx and ARTEX both on the host** (binary, `./start.sh`): the peer is `127.0.0.1`; start ARTEX with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1/32`. - **nginx on the host, ARTEX in Docker** (`docker-compose.yml`): the connection reaches the container from the Docker bridge gateway (a `172.x` address), not from `127.0.0.1`. Find it with `docker network inspect artex_default --format '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` (the network is `_default`), put `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=/32` in `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`. For a peer in that list, ARTEX reads `X-Forwarded-For` from the right and takes the first address that is not a trusted proxy; from any other peer the header is ignored. Trust only proxies you run: a trusted peer can claim any client address. > Only when SSE needs a different origin from the page (e.g. a dedicated subdomain) should you set > `NEXT_PUBLIC_SSE_BASE` **at build time** (it is baked into the static bundle during `next build`; > setting it at container runtime has no effect). --- ## Operations ### Troubleshooting an empty tool call In the task's session transcript, expand the affected tool call and compare **Command** and **Output**. The `UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT` markers identify the boundary around tool output. They are expected and should stay enabled while troubleshooting. - **Command shows `{}`.** The recorded tool input is an empty JSON object. For a tool that requires a command, this means its command argument was missing. Check which model and version produced the call. - **Command shows `(empty)` or `(failed to load)`.** The transcript has no input detail to display or could not fetch it. If the session record contains a command, include that discrepancy in a report. - **Output shows `[]`.** This is the recorded result body. Check the row's success or failure indicator and its input separately before drawing conclusions about what ran. For a recurring problem, share the ARTEX version or commit, the model and version, and a sanitized excerpt of the affected input and result. Remove credentials, target data, and other sensitive content before sharing. ### Backups `scripts/backup.sh` dumps the Postgres database (and optionally the data directory) with timestamped output and rotation: ```bash scripts/backup.sh --with-data # db dump + data/ archive, keep 14 scripts/backup.sh --keep 7 # db only, keep 7 ``` Restore into a running stack: ```bash gunzip -c backups/artex-db-.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \ psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" ``` Stored secrets (LLM API keys and proxies, MCP env, task credentials, notification channel config, Brave/Tavily search keys, web search and global proxies, the execution spec of custom tools, the capture-proxy rewrite rules) are encrypted in the database with the key in `keys/secret.key` (generated at first start, mode 0600, next to `jwt.key`). **A database backup without that key cannot restore those secrets**: back up `keys/` with the dump, separately. Deployments without a persistent disk set `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY` (32 bytes, base64 or hex, e.g. `openssl rand -base64 32`). ARTEX refuses to start when the database holds encrypted secrets and no key is available. Daily cron example (03:20, operator crontab): ``` 20 3 * * * cd /path/to/ARTEX && scripts/backup.sh --with-data >> backups/backup.log 2>&1 ``` ### Updating and upgrading > Upgrading swaps the program and never touches data: the Postgres volume `pgdata`, `./data` > (traffic index, task files, transcripts), `./keys` (`jwt.key`, `secret.key`) and `./skills` are > preserved. **No manual database step is needed**: on every start ARTEX applies its embedded > `schema.sql` baseline, then any pending numbered migration from `db/migrations/`, in order, each > in its own transaction. Restarting the new binary is the upgrade. Back up `./data`, `keys/` and > the database before upgrading. **Update banner (opt-in, off by default)**: start ARTEX with `ARTEX_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to ask the public GitHub releases API for the latest tag, at most once per 24 hours (cached in memory; a failed check is not retried within that window). When the release is newer, the web UI shows a dismissible strip linking to Releases. The request sends only `User-Agent: artex-update-check`. Unset, ARTEX makes no update request and shows no banner. #### Upgrading from a clone made before 2026-10-23 The repository history was rewritten that day to drop a personal email address from the commit metadata. A clone made before then cannot fast-forward, and `./update.sh` now stops instead of silently rebuilding stale code. Recover once, then upgrade normally: ```bash git stash # only if you have local changes git fetch origin git reset --hard origin/main git stash pop # only if you stashed ``` Your data is unaffected: `./data`, the `pgdata` volume and `./skills` are not part of git history. #### Option 1: one-click update script ```bash cd ARTEX ./update.sh ``` The script optionally `git pull`s, then offers **① Docker update** (`docker compose build artex` → `docker compose up -d artex`) or **② local build update** (rebuild the frontend static assets, then recompile `./artex`; restart the process for it to take effect). #### Option 2: Docker Compose (manual) ```bash cd ARTEX git pull docker compose build artex docker compose up -d artex docker image prune -f # optional ``` #### Option 3: prebuilt binaries Download the new zip, stop the old process, overwrite `artex` and `skills/` (keep `config.json` and `data/`), then restart: ```bash cp -r /skills ./ && cp /artex ./ ./start.sh ``` #### Option 4: build from source ```bash git pull cd web && npm ci && npm run build:static && cd .. cp -r web/out server/webui/dist CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags embedui -o artex ./cmd/artex # restart ./start.sh ``` --- ## Development ```bash ./dev.sh # backend(:8787) + traffic proxy(:8788) + frontend next dev(:5173) → http://localhost:5173 ``` - Backend: `go run ./cmd/artex` (without `-tags embedui`, the frontend is not embedded) - Frontend: `cd web && npm run dev` (`/api` is reverse-proxied to the backend, with hot reload) - Tests: `go test ./...` - Reproduce all CI checks locally: `./scripts/verify.sh` (add `--full` for `-race` and the static web build) - Mock preview (no backend): `cd web && NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK=1 npm run dev` --- ## Architecture ARTEX is an **LLM multi-agent-driven autonomous penetration testing system**: a Go monolithic backend (with the Next.js UI embedded) + PostgreSQL. Agent capabilities come from the [`norma`](https://github.com/Autumn-27/norma) SDK (`agentcore` / `tool` / `permission` / `harness` / `memory` / `transcript`). At its core is the **dual-graph architecture**, plus two autonomy mechanisms: **process-level information exchange between workers** and the **planner's multi-round shared todolist**. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph FE["Frontend Next.js (go:embed embedded single binary)"] UI["Dashboard · Tasks · Assets · Coverage graph · Traffic · Workspace · System settings"] end subgraph SRV["server (Go net/http)"] API["REST /api/* JWT auth SSE"] ENG["engine scheduling loop"] MGR["Manager task/engine/store lifecycle"] end subgraph AG["agent (norma SDK)"] GO["goals goal decomposition + scope extraction"] PL["planner the planner (sole intent generator)"] WK["worker executor ×N"] MA["mainagent human-in-the-loop"] end subgraph DB["PostgreSQL"] AGRAPH["Asset graph assets / companies / task_scope"] EGRAPH["Exploration graph exploration_nodes / anchors / activity"] end subgraph SUB["Supporting subsystems"] PROXY["Traffic recording proxy MITM + CA tracing"] GUARD["guard / intercept tool approval gate"] ENR["enrich DNS / HTTP async enrichment"] EXT["MCP · skills · memory · report"] end UI -->|HTTP| API API --> MGR --> ENG ENG --> PL ENG --> WK API --> MA API --> GO PL --> DB WK --> DB MA --> DB GO --> DB WK -->|"Bash / HTTP fully traced"| PROXY WK --> GUARD WK --> ENR PL -.-> EXT WK -.-> EXT MA -.-> EXT ``` | Layer | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | **Frontend** | Next.js static export embedded via `go:embed`; tasks, assets, exploration and coverage graphs, traffic, human-in-the-loop chat | | **server** | `net/http` routing, JWT auth, SSE; `Manager` owns tasks, engines and DB stores | | **engine** | One `plannerLoop` + N worker goroutines per task; intent claiming, timeout/pause/drain | | **agent** | goals / planner / worker / mainagent; `ToolSet` exposes the dual graphs as LLM tools | | **db** | PostgreSQL persistence (pgx); embedded schema and numbered migrations applied at startup | | **Supporting** | Recording MITM proxy, approval gate, async enrichment, MCP/skills/memory/report | For the code-level map (execution flow, trust boundaries, decisions) see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); for startup, configuration precedence, backup and key rotation see [docs/OPS.md](docs/OPS.md). --- ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub Security Advisories; see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Operational security properties: - **Secrets at rest**: LLM keys/proxies, MCP environment, task credentials, notification config, search keys, proxies, custom-tool execution specs, capture-proxy rewrite rules and traffic evidence snapshots are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using `keys/secret.key` (or `ARTEX_SECRET_KEY`). ARTEX refuses to start when encrypted data exists and no usable key is available. - **First-run claim**: `/setup` requires a one-time token printed at startup; the UI binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. - **Login protection**: 10 attempts per minute per client IP, with `ARTEX_TRUSTED_PROXIES` for correct client attribution behind a reverse proxy. - **Untrusted tool output**: framed as data for every agent by default (prompt-injection boundary). - **Release integrity**: SHA-256 sums, CycloneDX SBOM and GitHub build provenance attestations for release archives. --- ## About this fork This repository is the English translation and continuation of ARTEX, originally by [Autumn-27](https://github.com/Autumn-27). The upstream repository is no longer public, so the link points to the author profile. The frontier models are just there — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and the rest. > Free, with no usage cap.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：386179533（OFM技术交流群[1群]）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 [OpenCode 的 Zen 网关](https://opencode.ai)，Kilo 渠道来源为 [Kilo AI 的公共网关](https://kilo.ai)，均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——两类模型两种控制：声明了思考档位的模型（如 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、GLM 5.3 Flash）给出它自己的档位菜单（Off / Low / High / Max 等），选中值按原值下发到上游 `reasoning_effort`，上游会校验该字段、集合外的取值直接 400；没有档位菜单的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）走预算阶梯——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，思考不可关闭的模型三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度。两者都逐次调用留痕，设置页每张模型卡均标注档位或该档实际下发的上限（详见「思考强度：档位菜单与预算阶梯」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。Chat 历史中 assistant 的字符串 `reasoning_content` 会随工具后续请求保留，包括显式空字符串；缺失字段不会被补造。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 76 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI、FleetRelay Gateway，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十个账号渠道，一体接入**——LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **视觉特效按需开启**——设置页顶部“视觉特效”开关默认关闭，鱼缸和业务功能始终保留；开启后恢复背景光晕、毛玻璃与装饰动画，选择仅保存在当前浏览器。 - **OFM 插件中心：渠道 / 增强 / 页面统一市场**——新仓库 分组下的任意模型。选择结果按会话持久化。 **调整思考强度**：同一菜单中的 Effort。声明了思考档位的模型给出它自己的档位（如 Off / Low / High / Max），选中值按原值下发；其余模型给 Light / Balanced / Deep 三档，档位越高思考占用的 输出预算越多，上限为强制下发，因此档位之间存在可测量的差异。思考与可见回答共享同一输出额度， 规则通常在数百毫秒内释放），仍被占用则顺延至下一个可用端口，并在设置页标注 "请求的 18899 不可用，实际监听 18900"，落盘的也是该实际端口。Windows 上最常见的占用 来源是一条 netsh interface portproxy 规则（由 IP Helper 服务承载）：其对 0.0.0.0 的 监听会导致回环绑定直接返回 EACCES（区别于 EADDRINUSE）。netsh interface portproxy show all 可列出规则，netsh interface portproxy reset 可清除规则。 转发端点为全流式：除 `data:` 帧外，思考期间的静默由周期性写出的 SSE 注释帧 （以 `:` 开头）填充，客户端的 idle 超时因此不会将"上游仍在推理"误判为"连接已断开"。思考内容按 插件将已收到的思考作为检查点文本，与原始输入一起发起新请求，要求直接输出整理后的回答。 该机制基于检查点重新发起请求，与上游原生 resume 无关，也不会重放已显示的思考内容。恢复段禁用工具调用；已输出 正文或已开始调用工具的截断回合不执行恢复，以避免内容重复或工具重复执行。 为避免重复长思考，恢复提示要求结论优先、最多 800 词；此为提示层面的约束（非硬性 token 限制），模型可能不遵守。恢复属于降级回答，原始请求中的长篇或逐步分析可能被简化。 每个逻辑回合最多两次物理请求：原始请求加一次恢复。默认总时限 900 秒（15 分钟），恢复段最多 300 秒，且受剩余总时长约束；恢复输出上限 8192 tokens，并继续受用户与模型的上限 约束。首段已知的输出 tokens 会从原始预算中扣除，恢复预算不足 512 tokens 时不发起恢复。 检查点最多 131072 字符，且必须通过基于文本字节的保守上下文余量估算；该估算不计算图片 token，不等同于精确的 tokenizer 校验。超出限制即停止恢复，不会无限续接。恢复必须正常结束且 产生非空白正文方为成功；失败返回 STREAM_CUT，宿主不会将该回合整轮重发，用户取消 则保持 aborted / ABORTED。 可通过本机 settings.json 的 streamRecovery: false 关闭恢复；也可通过对象的 enabled 开关及数值限制收窄边界，数值只能低于或等于默认上限。默认不限制模型名单。 用量看板将物理请求与逻辑回合分开统计。上游请求数与请求失败数按实际发出的请求次数计数； 对话回合数、回合失败数与已恢复数按一次适配器调用的最终结果计数。例如首段中断、 续写成功会记为 2 次上游请求、1 次请求失败，同时记为 1 加密密封：渠道凭据与端点从不以可读形式出现在插件中——它们仅以 AES-256-GCM 密文存在，解密密钥由分散在两个文件中的三片掩码分片在解锁时即时派生；非授权宿主不进入派生路径，密文对搜索引擎与字符串扫描而言仅为噪声。 凭据不落盘、不出进程：解锁按请求即时发生，明文仅存在于构造请求的那一帧中，不写入文件、不进入日志、不出现在任何 API 响应或错误消息中。 签名网关（推荐形态）：worker/ 目录附带一个 Cloudflare Worker 网关——插件密封的仅有网关地址与 HMAC 签名密钥，请求按 时间戳 + HMAC-SHA256(方法/路径/ body 摘要) 签名，中继的真实 key 仅存放于 Worker 的环境变量中；防重放时间窗、模型白名单、可选按 IP 限速均在网关执行，签名密钥泄露只需在网关侧轮换即可全体吊销。部署与轮换见 worker/README.md。 **GitHub 授权闸门**：自建网关（宝塔 Node 形态）另带一道按人计的授权闸门——对话请求除签名外还需携带一枚**专属令牌**，而令牌只发给「用 GitHub 登录 + 已 star 本仓库」的账号。登录全程在浏览器里完成：设置页「EAC 渠道授权」一键发起，网关回调页确认 star 状态后签发令牌，插件自动领取，无需复制粘贴；未 star 时页面会给出 ⭐ 按钮与「我已 star，重新检查」，不必重新登录。网关默认每 12 小时用保存的授权复查一次 star，取消 star 即在复查窗口内吊销令牌；GitHub 侧不可达时保留既有判定，不会误伤已授权用户。网关只申请 `read:user` 最小权限，授权仅用于 star 复查。免费车道（opencode）不经过网关，完全不受影响。 ## 上游是哪些源 两条公开免密来源，均直连、不经任何第三方中转；另有第四条出网目标为自建网关（EAC 渠道，见其专节）。 **免费车道：OpenCode 的免密网关，https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/\***（2026-10-14 从 `/zen/v1` 迁到这里；旧路径对免费模型一律 403 FreeTierError）。 具体到代码——src/upstream.js 中每一条均通过直接请求核对（路径与指纹：2026-10-14 / 10-16）： | 用途 | 目标 | 携带何种凭据 | | --- | --- | --- | | 推理请求 | POST …/inference/v1/chat/completions、…/inference/v1/responses、…/inference/v1/messages（按模型分流，见 endpointFor） | Authorization: Bearer public——该车道本身即为公开免密额度，插件中不含任何属于你的密钥 | | 模型清单 | GET …/inference/v1/models | 同上 | | 公告与升级清单 | 本仓库的 feed/\*.json：raw.githubusercontent.com 优先，cdn.jsdelivr.net 兜底 | 无 | | 出口地区判定 | api.ipify.org / ipinfo.io / ipapi.co，仅用于读取本机公网 IP 与国家码 | 无 | **Kilo 渠道：Kilo AI 的公共网关，https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway**（2026-10-06 接入）。 代码在 src/kilo.js，每一条均于接入当日通过直接请求核对： | 用途 | 目标 | 携带何种凭据 | | --- | --- | --- | | 推理请求 | POST …/api/gateway/chat/completions（OpenAI Chat Completions 兼容，SSE 流式） | **无**——该网关的免费池（清单中 `isFree: true` 的模型，含 kilo-auto/free 自动路由）不需任何账号、Key 或登录态 | | 模型清单 | GET …/api/gateway/models | 无 | 关于隐私与信任，说明如下： 没有号池、没有中转、没有二道贩子。上表即为本插件全部出网目标；npm test 的离线套件完全不出网（共享测试脚手架会把两条免密来源都默认指向已关闭的本机端口，杜绝任何套件"顺带"打到真实网关），仅 scripts/host-selftest.mjs 与 scripts/probes/ 会主动请求这些地址，且需手动运行。若将来引入新的来源，本节会先于功能更新，不会默认将流量分配给第三方。 你的 prompt、工具结果与随附图像会作为正常推理请求发送至所选模型对应的上游——与调用任何模型 API 相同。除此之外插件不上传任何内容：用量看板数据、设置、转发 Key 均只落在本机 DSH_HOME/our-free-model/。 免密不等于无人管理：免费车道通过 x-opencode-\* 指纹识别客户端、按会话统计免费额度，会因地区返回 403、因超量返回 429。**Kilo 免费池在其模型卡中明确声明：prompt 可能被上游提供方记录，并用于改进其服务**（原文见 kilo-auto/free 模型卡："Prompts may be logged by the upstream provider and used to improve their services. Not suitable for production or sensitive data workloads."）。模型集合与额度政策由上游决定，随时可能变更；插件仅能如实将不可用的模型从选择器中移除。 本节属于仓库文档。应用内的选择器、设置页与报错文案中仍不出现上游厂名（该约定见验收情况一节），但 Kilo 渠道的模型卡徽章悬停提示会告知"prompt 可能被上游记录"——这是选择模型时需要知道的信息。 ## 免责声明 - **本插件是一个客户端，不是模型服务方。** 所有模型响应均由上述第三方上游（OpenCode Zen 网关、Kilo AI 公共网关、以及你自己部署的 EAC 网关）生成并传输；插件不托管、不修改、不过滤任何模型输出。模型可能产出错误、过时或有偏颇的内容，请自行核实后再使用。 - **免费不等于无限，也不等于私有。** 免费额度由上游单方面提供，随时可能限流、收费或下线；Kilo 免费池明确声明 prompt 可能被上游记录并用于改进服务。**请勿通过本插件的免费车道发送密码、密钥、个人身份信息、商业机密或任何你不愿第三方处理的内容**；生产与敏感场景请使用你自己的付费 API。 - **上游条款由你遵守。** 使用各渠道即表示你同意对应上游的服务条款与用量政策；因违反上游政策导致的限流、封禁或其它后果由使用者自行承担。插件不对任何上游的可用性、准确性或连续性作任何承诺。 - **EAC 渠道为协付性质。** 该渠道的凭据与网关由仓库维护者部署（GitHub 登录 + star 仓库解锁），仅限授权用户使用；请勿尝试绕过授权闸门，勿转售或共享渠道访问权——滥用会导致全体用户的通道被收紧。 - **本插件与上述任何上游厂商无隶属或背书关系。** 各厂商名称与商标归其各自所有者所有，仅在说明来源时引用。 ## 安全与隐私 所有状态写入 DSH_HOME/our-free-model/；用量与设置仅落在本机，不上传至任何位置。 聚合车道的 Key 同样不出本机：它只写入插件自己的 0600 `settings.json`，请求只发往你自己配置的那家提供商，插件接口只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹，从不回显 Key 本身；测试与发现模型两次探测也把回包中的 Key 一律脱敏。 转发监听仅绑定回环地址，默认 127.0.0.1，无 Key 请求一律拒绝。将地址改为可路由接口会被直接拒绝（POST /settings 返回 400 并注明原因；在无 web server 的 composition 中手工写入 settings.json 同样不会启动监听）——该端口的流量消耗的是本机这条免密车道，不应由一个字符串决定是否向整个子网开放。 局域网访问是另开的一扇门，并不放宽上述规则：本机监听仍只绑回环、修改地址仍被拒绝；需要跨机器使用时必须显式启用"局域网访问"，中继绑定可路由地址，且每个请求都需携带局域网 Key——连 /、/health 这类存活探针也一并鉴权（仅本机监听免 Key 应答存活探测），否则一个未鉴权的应答等同于向整个子网宣告"该主机正在代理"。中继仅转发 /v1/models、/v1/chat/completions、/v1/responses、/v1/messages、/v1/messages/count_tokens 五条白名单路径（各自的去 /v1 写法同样放行），不代理任意 loopback 服务；入口处将局域网 Key 换为本机 Key，因此两把 Key 互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。本仓库不含任何硬编码凭据。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经 dns.lookup 解析、全部结果均为回环才放行，绑定使用解析出的 IP——当 hosts 文件或企业 DNS 将 localhost 指向可路由接口时，校验与监听不再各自为政。 卸载只需移除 bundle 条目，插件不留任何补丁；其数据目录为纯 JSON，可直接删除。 ## 许可证 本仓库自己的代码是 MIT，见 LICENSE。第三方组件和数据的许可证见下一节「致谢」。 本项目为独立插件，与任何模型提供方无隶属、认可或赞助关系。使用该插件访问免费额度受各提供方 自身条款约束；在超出个人机器的场景中部署前，请先确认这些条款。 ## 致谢 感谢 Jet（iJetLi）的渠道包（`vendor/channel-pack/`，MIT；上游仓库 [dsh-providers-hub](https://github.com/iJetLi/dsh-providers-hub)）—— 十个内置账号渠道的登录、账号池与本地网关都出自这里，许可证与出处见该目录下的 LICENSE 与 NOTICE.md。 也感谢这些项目的代码或数据： - [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api)（GPL-3.0）：历史免费车道请求整形来源；2.8.6 的实现变化和已删除资产见 [维护说明](src/o2a/SYNC.md)。 - [free-claude-code](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code)（AGPL-3.0-only）：历史供应商目录及五个本地应答的来源；2.8.6 重写本地应答并重建目录，历史 ID 的处理见 [兼容说明](docs/provider-compatibility.md)。 - [9router](https://github.com/decolua/9router)（MIT）：部分提供商目录，以及免费车道的请求形状参考。 - [models.dev](https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev)（MIT）：模型窗口、输出上限与思考档位。 - [trae-mate](https://github.com/luckymiaow/trae-mate)（MIT）：TRAE 签到流程参考。 - [dsh-cline-pass](https://github.com/codeOct/dsh-cline-pass)（MIT）：Cline 额度与请求记录参考。 - [rtk](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk)（CLI Apache-2.0，engine BUSL-1.1）：工具输出过滤器的历史参考；2.8.6 的替换范围和行为对照见 [验证记录](docs/verification/2026-11-18-independent-core.md)。 - [magpie-muse-web](https://github.com/JohnWangggg/magpie-muse-web)（上游未声明 SPDX 许可证）：`muse-web` 桥接扩展的上游。 根目录的 MIT 只覆盖 OFM 自己写的代码；上面这些组件和数据按各自许可证提供，完整条款以上游 LICENSE 为准。这份名单是来源记录，不改变任何组件的许可证。 ## Star 趋势 图表由 Star History 自动更新，无需手动提交图片。受服务缓存（当前为 24 小时）和 GitHub 图片缓存影响，显示可能延迟，并非秒级实时；点击图表可查看在线趋势。

Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. ## Quick start **[Get started at rea.tools](https://rea.tools/get-started/)** for step-by-step instructions by operating system, agent, and analysis provider. ### Connect your agent (MCP) With [Node.js and npm](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) installed, run this from a trusted directory outside the project you plan to analyze. ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agent, review and approve the setup plan, then restart your agent. Setup backs up existing configuration and adds REA's MCP connection and investigation skill. See the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for supported clients, plugins, manual registration, and troubleshooting. Try asking your agent: ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use REA from the terminal (CLI) Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. The [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) covers provider selection, native commands, snapshots, and scripting. For Linux prerequisites, see the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md#linux-owned-process-prerequisite). ### Update REA For a global npm or Bun installation, run the updater and follow its setup instructions. ```bash rea update ``` If you use `npx`, refresh your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. See [update and uninstall instructions](docs/getting-started/installation.md#diagnose-update-and-remove) for package runner options and troubleshooting. ## Showcases

DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation

Recover a position-to-pan helper from x86 instructions and verify the C reconstruction against 3,205 original-x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository

Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge

Follow the renderer’s clipboard API through preload and IPC into the main process to see how Notion handles rich clipboard data.

Read the case study

TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation

Recover fixed and aimed angle calculations from the PC-98 game’s 16-bit instructions and compare the reconstructed C++ with historical compiler output.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository
If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## How REA works Your agent uses REA through MCP to inspect a target and trace the relevant code. It can use the evidence REA returns to ask follow-up questions, explain behavior, or build and test an implementation. The CLI uses the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA covers native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, websites, .NET assemblies, Android apps, firmware, and recorded runtime and network activity. [Supported targets and requirements](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) For native decompilation, choose a provider that supports your target format and host OS. See [choosing a deep analysis provider](docs/reference/supported-targets.md#choosing-a-deep-analysis-provider). ## Build RL environments Build a local environment from a recorded web session or a Linux desktop app so an agent can practice a task and check its result. [Build an RL environment with REA](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/). ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.

# Superpowers

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## Table of Contents

- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Commercial Services](#commercial-services)
- [Getting Started](#installation)
  - [Claude Code](#claude-code)
  - [Antigravity](#antigravity)
  - [Codex App](#codex-app)
  - [Codex CLI](#codex-cli)
  - [Cursor](#cursor)
  - [Devin CLI](#devin-cli)
  - [Factory Droid](#factory-droid)
  - [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli)
  - [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli)
  - [Grok Build CLI](#grok-build-cli)
  - [Kimi Code](#kimi-code)
  - [OpenCode](#opencode)
  - [Pi](#pi)
  - [Qwen Code](#qwen-code)
  - [Hermes Agent](#hermes-agent)
  - [Muse](#muse)
- [The Basic Workflow](#the-basic-workflow)
- [When Something Goes Wrong](#when-something-goes-wrong)
- [Community](#community)
- [What's Inside](#whats-inside)
- [Philosophy](#philosophy)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Updating](#updating)
- [License](#license)
- [Visual companion telemetry](#visual-companion-telemetry)

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

## Commercial Services

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

## Installation

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

### Claude Code

Superpowers is available via the [official Claude plugin marketplace](https://claude.com/plugins/superpowers)

#### Official Marketplace

- Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
  ```

#### Superpowers Marketplace

The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin from this marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Antigravity

Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

```bash
agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
```

Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the `using-superpowers` skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

### Codex App

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.
- You should see `Superpowers` in the Coding section.
- Click the `+` next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

### Codex CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- Open the plugin search interface:

  ```bash
  /plugins
  ```

- Search for Superpowers:

  ```bash
  superpowers
  ```

- Select `Install Plugin`.

### Cursor

- In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

  ```text
  /add-plugin superpowers
  ```

- Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

### Devin CLI

- Install the plugin from this repository:

  ```bash
  devin plugins install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update to the latest version with:

  ```bash
  devin plugins update superpowers
  ```

### Factory Droid

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers
  ```

### Gemini CLI

- Install the extension:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions update superpowers
  ```

### GitHub Copilot CLI

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Grok Build CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Grok plugin marketplace](https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace).

- Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust
  ```

- Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

  ```text
  /marketplace
  ```

### Kimi Code

Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

- Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

  ```text
  /plugins
  ```

- Go to `Marketplace` > `Superpowers` and install it.

- Or install directly from this repository:

  ```text
  /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.kimi.md](docs/README.kimi.md)

### OpenCode

OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

- Tell OpenCode:

  ```
  Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.opencode.md](docs/README.opencode.md)

### Pi

Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

```bash
pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers
```

For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

```bash
pi -e /path/to/superpowers
```

The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility `Skill` tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

### Qwen Code

Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

- Install the plugin from this repository, and pick `superpowers` when prompted:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions update superpowers
  ```

### Hermes Agent

Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

```bash
hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable
```

Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

### Muse

Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The `using-superpowers` bootstrap is injected via the native `SessionStart` hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

- Install from a local checkout:

  ```bash
  muse plugins install ./
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

  Or clone and install:

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
  muse plugins install ./superpowers
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  muse plugins update superpowers
  ```

Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the `SessionStart` hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send `Let's make a react todo list` — a working install auto-triggers `brainstorming` before any code is written. Version is tracked in `.version-bump.json` so `scripts/bump-version.sh` keeps it in sync.

## The Basic Workflow

1. **brainstorming** - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

2. **using-git-worktrees** - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

3. **writing-plans** - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

4. **subagent-driven-development** or **executing-plans** - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

5. **test-driven-development** - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

6. **requesting-code-review** - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

7. **finishing-a-development-branch** - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

**The agent checks for relevant skills before any task.** Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

## When Something Goes Wrong

Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the **diagnosing-superpowers** skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session `<id>`".

The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

## Community

Superpowers is built by [Jesse Vincent](https://blog.fsck.com) and the rest of the folks at [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com).

- **Discord**: [Join us](https://discord.gg/35wsABTejz) for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers
- **Issues**: https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues
- **Release announcements**: [Sign up](https://primeradiant.com/superpowers/) to get notified about new versions

## What's Inside

### Skills Library

**Testing**
- **test-driven-development** - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

**Debugging**
- **systematic-debugging** - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)
- **verification-before-completion** - Ensure it's actually fixed
- **diagnosing-superpowers** - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

**Collaboration** 
- **brainstorming** - Drawing out intent before building
- **writing-plans** - Detailed implementation plans
- **executing-plans** - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review
- **dispatching-parallel-agents** - Concurrent subagent workflows
- **requesting-code-review** - Pre-review checklist
- **receiving-code-review** - Responding to feedback
- **using-git-worktrees** - Parallel development branches
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - Merge/PR decision workflow
- **subagent-driven-development** - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

**Meta**
- **writing-skills** - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)
- **using-superpowers** - Introduction to the skills system

## Philosophy

- **Test-Driven Development** - Write tests first, always
- **Systematic over ad-hoc** - Process over guessing
- **Complexity reduction** - Simplicity as primary goal
- **Evidence over claims** - Verify before declaring success

Read [the original release announcement](https://blog.fsck.com/2025/10/09/superpowers/).

## Contributing

The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

1. Fork the repository
2. Switch to the 'dev' branch
3. Create a branch for your work
4. Follow the `writing-skills` skill for creating and testing new and modified skills
5. Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the summary a human writes in their own words.

Skill-behavior tests use the drill eval harness from [superpowers-evals](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/superpowers-evals/), cloned into `evals/` — see `evals/README.md` for setup. Plugin-infrastructure tests live at `tests/` and run via the relevant `run-*.sh` or `npm test`.

See `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md` for the complete guide.

## Updating

Superpowers updates are somewhat coding-agent dependent, but are often automatic.

## License

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details

## Visual companion telemetry

Because skills and plugins don't provide any feedback to creators, we have no idea how many of you are using Superpowers. By default, the Prime Radiant logo on brainstorming's optional visual companion feature is loaded from our website. It includes the version of Superpowers in use. It does not include any details about your project, prompt, or coding agent. We don't see your clicks or anything about what you're building. This helps us have a rough idea of how many folks are using Superpowers and which version of Superpowers they're using. It's 100% optional. To disable this, set the environment variable `SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` to any true value. Superpowers also honors Claude Code's `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` opt-outs.

# Google QR SMS Helper (`google-qr-sms-helper`)

将 Google 桌面端强制跨设备扫码验证（MO-SMS / GMS Constellation）一键降级回传统的「输入手机号接收 6 位短信验证码」流程。
Switch Google's mandatory cross-device QR verification back to standard 6-digit SMS / Voice verification on desktop browsers.

--- ## 📦 一、安装教程 (Installation) ### 方式 1：直接下载 Release 压缩包（推荐新手） 1. 前往本仓库的 **[Releases 页面](https://github.com/havenicec/google-qr-sms-helper/releases/latest)**，下载最新的 `google-qr-sms-helper-v1.1.0.zip` 并解压到本地文件夹。 2. 打开 Chrome / Edge / Brave 浏览器，在地址栏输入 `chrome://extensions/` 并回车。 3. 打开页面右上角的 **「开发者模式 (Developer mode)」** 开关。 4. 点击左上角的 **「加载已解压的扩展程序 (Load unpacked)」**，选中刚才解压出来的文件夹即可完成安装。 ### 方式 2：通过 Git 克隆安装 ```bash git clone https://github.com/havenicec/google-qr-sms-helper.git ``` 然后在 `chrome://extensions/` 中开启「开发者模式」，点击「加载已解压的扩展程序」并选择 `google-qr-sms-helper` 目录。 --- ## 🚀 二、保姆级图文使用教程 (Step-by-Step Usage Guide) > [!IMPORTANT] > **核心前提（必看）**：**不要**直接从第三方客户端（如 Antigravity / Gemini Code Assist 授权页）弹出的二维码页面降级（因为其 `continue` 参数包含多层嵌套重定向，会被 Google 重新拦截回二维码）。 > **必须先打开 Google Cloud Console 通过 Cloud Shell 唤出原生的 `Verify` 窗口**！在这里过完一次短信验证后，你的 Google 账号权限将全局解锁，再回 Antigravity 等工具登录即可直接丝滑通过。 ### 第 1 步：打开 Google Cloud Console 并唤起 Cloud Shell 验证 1. 在浏览器中登录你需要验证的 Google 账号，访问 **[https://console.cloud.google.com/](https://console.cloud.google.com/)**。 2. 如下图所示，点击页面右上角导航栏的 **「激活 Cloud Shell」终端图标 `[>_]`**（或者直接点击页面右下角插件悬浮窗里的 **`1. 自动点击 Cloud Shell 终端图标`** 按钮）。 3. 在底部弹出的 `Verify your account` 窗口中，点击蓝色的 **`Verify`** 按钮： ![Cloud Shell Verify 入口示意](./assets/cloud-shell-verify.png) --- ### 第 2 步：在二维码页面点击「一键降级到短信选择框」 1. 点击 `Verify` 后，会弹出 Google 的二维码验证页面（`/v3/signin/challenge/iap/qrcode`）。 2. 等待二维码图片加载出来后，点击页面右下角插件悬浮面板上的 **「⚡ 一键降级到短信选择框」** 按钮： - 插件会自动调用浏览器原生 `BarcodeDetector` 识别页面上的二维码； - 自动在后台向 Google 发送 `MypxBd` 与 `YDtwf ([null, uuid, dsh, 7, null, tl, false])` 数据包，拿到 `[3, null, 4]`（非 Android 设备回退短信验证状态）； - 自动将当前标签页的请求头与环境伪装为 **`iPad Mini`**（无需手动按 F12 切换设备），并重定向到 `uplevelingstep/selection?...&idv_xdevice=1`。 --- ### 第 3 步：选择「短信 (Text message)」并输入手机号接码 1. 页面会自动跳转进带有单选框的 **验证方式选择页 (`/uplevelingstep/selection`)**： - 勾选 **Text message (SMS) / 短信**（或语音通话），点击下一步。 2. 在手机号输入框中填入你的接码手机号（支持任意国家/地区的接码平台号码或实体卡号），点击发送验证码。 3. 收到 `G-xxxxxx` 的 6 位数字验证码后填入并点击 **Next**，即可完成账号验证！ 4. 验证通过后，回到 Cloud Shell 或 Antigravity / Gemini CLI 刷新即可正常使用。 --- ## ❓ 三、常见问题与避坑指南 (FAQ & Troubleshooting) ### Q1: 为什么我从别的链接点进二维码页，点降级后又跳回了二维码？ - **原因**：只有从 `https://console.cloud.google.com/` 点击右上角 **Cloud Shell `[>_]` -> `Verify`** 唤出的二维码页，其 `continue` 参数才是纯净的 `https://accounts.google.com/uplevelingstep/selection?TL=...&authuser=0&flowName=GlifWebSignIn&sarp=1&scc=1`。请务必按「第 1 步」从 Cloud Shell 入口进入。 ### Q2: 为什么插件默认伪装成 `iPad Mini` 而不是 `iPad Pro` 或桌面浏览器？ - **原因**：Google 的 `uplevelingstep/selection` 接口会校验 `User-Agent`： - 桌面端（Windows / macOS）以及 Chrome F12 中的 `iPad Pro 13` 发送的都是 `Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X` 桌面级 UA，Google 检测到桌面环境会无视 `idv_xdevice=1` 强行跳回二维码。 - 而 `iPad Mini` 发送的是纯移动端 `iPad; CPU OS 16_6 like Mac OS X ... Mobile/15E148` 请求头，且在提交 6 位验证码的 `/_/IdvUplevelingUi/data/batchexecute` 接口上必须保持前后完全一致的 `iPad Mini` 请求头（已在 v1.1.0 中通过 `declarativeNetRequest` 全路径自动覆盖，无需手动开 F12）。 ### Q3: 点击「一键降级」提示“未能在当前页面识别到二维码”怎么办？ - 请确认使用的是 **Chrome / Edge 88+** 浏览器（支持原生 `BarcodeDetector` 接口），并等待页面上的黑色二维码图案完全显示后再点击按钮。 --- ## ✨ 四、技术原理与工作流 (Architecture & Workflow) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as Desktop Browser (User) participant E as Extension (Content + DNR) participant B as Background Service Worker participant G as Google Identity Backend U->>G: 1. Click "⚡ 一键降级到短信选择框" E->>E: Decode QR Canvas/Image via native BarcodeDetector E->>B: Send QR URL (devicephoneverification/begin) B->>G: POST MypxBd (SelectNextVerificationMethod -> consent) B->>G: GET /devicephoneverification/consent (extract request UUID) B->>G: POST YDtwf [null, uuid, dsh, 7, null, tl, false] G-->>B: Return ["wrb.fr", "YDtwf", "[3, null, 4]"] (Non-Android Fallback) B-->>E: Fallback state locked E->>G: Redirect to uplevelingstep/selection?...&idv_xdevice=1 (with iPad Mini UA) G-->>U: Render SMS / Voice Radio Selection & 6-Digit Code Input ``` --- ## 📁 目录结构 (Project Structure) ```text google-qr-sms-helper/ ├── assets/ │ └── cloud-shell-verify.png # Cloud Shell Verify 入口示意图 ├── manifest.json # Chrome Extension Manifest V3 配置文件 ├── background.js # DNR 全路径 iPad Mini 请求头伪装 + [3,null,4] RPC 注入 ├── content.js # 悬浮控制面板 + BarcodeDetector 二维码识别 + URL 清洗跳转 ├── ua_spoof.js # Main-world navigator 属性对齐 ├── LICENSE # MIT 开源协议 └── README.md # 项目说明与图文教程 ``` --- ## 📄 License Released under the [MIT License](./LICENSE).
