![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **83 skills** · 15 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY
    

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 83 skills + 15 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 83 skills + 15 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **83 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 6 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 4 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **15 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — `triage-validation`'s 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The `bugcrowd-reporting` skill includes researcher-side hygiene (Bugcrowdninja alias, account-state restoration, friendly-tester posture) that signals legitimate authorized testing to the target's fraud team. The bundle explicitly **excludes**: weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full posture. > **Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards.** Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that **block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default** — so even *authorized, in-scope* work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's **free, application-based [Cyber Verification Program (CVP)](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case)** to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are *not* adjustable.) Details: [Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude). ### Why your model switched mid-session Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On **Opus 5**, a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names *exploit generation*, *binary-based vulnerability scanning* and *penetration testing* — **fall back to Opus 4.8** rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See [why Claude switched models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5). What to do depends on what you are actually doing: | Situation | What helps | |---|---| | **Auditing your own code** — reviewing a repo you own for defects | Say so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive. | | **Authorized offensive work** — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submission | This is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is [CVP](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case). Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead. | | **You just want the switching off** | Settings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching. | `/hunt` states the engagement frame (authorized, scope-bounded, remediable finding) on its first turn for exactly this reason — engagement context belongs in the session explicitly, not implied. --- ## Documentation | Doc | Contents | |---|---| | [`README.md`](README.md) | This file — overview, quickstart, scope, skill summary | | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) | Full setup with Burp MCP integration and optional skill regenerator | | [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) | Workflow walkthrough · decision tree · worked engagement example | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | 6-phase architecture · skill-to-phase mapping · engagement composition | | [`docs/cbh-cli.md`](docs/cbh-cli.md) | `cbh` CLI — native runner orchestrating recon + classify + triage + report | | [`docs/cve-coverage.md`](docs/cve-coverage.md) | CISA KEV coverage snapshot — refreshed weekly via the workflow template at `docs/automation/cve-refresh.yml.template` | | [`docs/credits.md`](docs/credits.md) | Full attribution: 43 original skills + 8 vendored from upstream | | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) | PR guidelines · skill quality standards · scope | | [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | Authorized-use posture · responsible disclosure · what's excluded | | [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) | MIT | | [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) | Upstream-skills attribution · no-redistribution note | | [`LICENSE-CONTENT`](LICENSE-CONTENT) | CC BY 4.0 (skill methodology, wordlists, docs) | --- ## Why this exists Most bug-hunting Claude setups are either too generic (one big "security" prompt) or too fragmented (you bookmark 30 disclosed reports and re-read them every engagement). Neither scales past the second target. This bundle was built and validated through authorized engagements that exposed different capability gaps: **Bug-bounty engagement** — surfaced four gaps a starter 3-skill stack could not close: 1. **No hypothesis discipline** — drafts written before validation → wasted hours, hurt validity ratio 2. **No per-program reporting tactics** — VRT defaults auto-downgraded P3-worthy findings to P4 3. **No engagement coordination** — findings, evidence, and submission IDs scattered across folders 4. **No evidence hygiene** — screenshots leaked cookies and victim PII **External red-team engagement** — exposed five additional gaps that bug-bounty defaults made worse: 1. **Conservative defaults retracted real findings** — WAPT mindset stopped tests early on defended targets where red-team continuation would have surfaced bypass chains → `redteam-mindset` 2. **No mid-engagement situational awareness** — client SOC patched confirmed SQLi within 30 min; external attacker locked 14 accounts during a live test session — both invisible without explicit detection methodology → `mid-engagement-ir-detection` 3. **No enterprise-platform attack chains** — M365 + Entra ID, on-prem SharePoint, Cisco SSL VPN, vCenter, and 7 Android APKs all needed current 2024-2026 CVE knowledge and platform-specific tradecraft → `m365-entra-attack`, `okta-attack`, `hunt-sharepoint`, `hunt-aspnet`, `hunt-ntlm-info`, `vmware-vcenter-attack`, `enterprise-vpn-attack`, `apk-redteam-pipeline` 4. **No client-facing deliverable format** — bug-bounty report templates don't fit enterprise red-team where output is a 50KB+ MD + DOCX with embedded screenshots → `redteam-report-template` 5. **No post-credential escalation model** — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate → `cloud-iam-deep` The per-class `hunt-*` skills address gap-zero (*"what should I look for in webapps"*) — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. The enterprise-platform and red-team-tradecraft layers address what bug-bounty alone cannot: external red-team engagements against monitored enterprise targets. --- ## Roadmap - [x] HackerOne MCP integration — [`mcp/hackerone/`](mcp/hackerone/README.md): disclosed-report duplicate search, program stats and scope; optional logged-in mode for private programs and your own reports - [ ] Per-engagement memory layer — pattern recall across targets - [x] Industry-specific hunt skills — `hunt-fintech-graphql` shipped; `hunt-healthcare-fhir`, `hunt-gov-compliance` still open - [ ] Program-rules-parser skill — auto-generate structured `scope.md` from program text - [ ] Refresh `hunt-*` skills with newer disclosed reports (re-run `public-skills-builder`) - [ ] Additional enterprise-platform skills — `citrix-netscaler-deep`, `f5-bigip-attack`, `ad-cs-attack` (AD Certificate Services) - [ ] Refresh enterprise-VPN CVE matrix quarterly to track 2026 advisories - [ ] Update architecture SVG to include the 7-skill enterprise-platform layer --- ## Sponsors

**[ApiSmart](https://www.apismart.ai/)** unifies leading LLM, image, and video models through one OpenAI-compatible API. Use one key to switch models, simplify billing, and improve reliability with automatic failover.

**[ThreatWatch360](https://threatwatch360.com)** is an AI-powered offensive-security platform: continuous Attack Surface Management, AI-assisted penetration testing, brand protection, dark-web monitoring, and Cyber Threat Intelligence in one platform. Validated findings with proof-of-concept and business-impact prioritization — signal over alert fatigue. --- ## About Operational tradecraft accumulated across bug-bounty engagements and authorized pentests, codified into Claude skills. Platform-agnostic — slot into any engagement workflow you already use, or none. **Author:** [ElementalSoul](https://github.com/elementalsouls) · GenAI Security Research **Sister project:** [Claude-OSINT](https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-OSINT) — paired skills for the recon phase that this bundle picks up after. Its two recon skills (`offensive-osint`, `osint-methodology`) are **canonically maintained here** and re-exported there, so the two are byte-identical. **Installing both is safe:** each bundle's installer (`install.sh` on macOS/Linux, `install.ps1` on Windows) records a manifest, the script skips re-copying an identical skill, and `--uninstall` keeps any skill the other bundle still owns — uninstalling one never breaks the other. **Vendored foundation:** [shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty](https://github.com/shuvonsec/claude-bug-bounty) — methodology, validation, reporting, payload library (8 of 83 skills + 15 slash commands) **Generator tool used (not vendored):** [shuvonsec/public-skills-builder](https://github.com/shuvonsec/public-skills-builder) — used to scaffold per-class skills from H1 disclosed reports **Inspirations:** - [archangel / douglasday](https://hackerone.com/) — top-10 H1 hunter; per-class skill pattern - [Trail of Bits — `trailofbits/skills`](https://github.com/trailofbits/skills) — skill-authoring discipline - [SecSkills — `trilwu/secskills`](https://github.com/trilwu/secskills) — subagent pattern **Tool inventory:** - [PortSwigger Burp Suite + MCP Server extension](https://portswigger.net/burp) - [ProjectDiscovery](https://github.com/projectdiscovery) — subfinder · dnsx · httpx · katana · nuclei - [SecLists](https://github.com/danielmiessler/SecLists) · [Assetnote Wordlists](https://wordlists.assetnote.io/) ## License This project is dual-licensed: - **Code** (Python helpers, shell scripts) — [MIT](LICENSE). - **Content** (skill methodology, wordlists, regex catalogs, severity rubrics, docs) — [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](LICENSE-CONTENT) (CC BY 4.0). --- # **🔥 Firecrawl** **Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three. - **[Firecrawl Local](#firecrawl-local).** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost. - **[Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud).** Use the hosted service at [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev/?ref=github) for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in [Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev) for far more knowledge than scraping alone. - **[Self-hosting](#self-hosting).** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure. _Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_ --- ## Firecrawl Local [Firecrawl Local](apps/local) scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`. ```bash cargo install firecrawl-local ``` If you don't have Rust, [Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud) runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup. ```bash npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev ``` Scrape a page and print its markdown. ```bash firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown ``` Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page. ```bash firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages ``` List every URL on a site. ```bash firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev ``` Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning. ### Add it to your AI agent `init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer. ```bash firecrawl-local init ``` Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud. ### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost `serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key. ```bash firecrawl-local serve ``` Point any Firecrawl SDK at it by setting the API URL. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_url="http://localhost:3002") print(app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev").markdown) ``` The [Firecrawl Local README](apps/local) covers every command and option, the security defaults for `serve` and running it in Docker. Move to [Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud) when you need structured JSON, Interact, the Agent or scale beyond one machine. --- ## What runs where | Feature | Firecrawl Local | Firecrawl Cloud | |---------|-----------------|-----------------| | [Scrape](#scrape) | Markdown, HTML, raw HTML and links | Adds structured JSON, summaries, screenshots and browser actions | | [Crawl](#crawl), [Map](#map) and [Batch Scrape](#batch-scrape) | ✅ | ✅ | | PDFs and Office documents | ✅ | ✅, plus [Parse](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/parse) for uploaded files | | [Search](#search) | Through Firecrawl Cloud, no account needed | ✅ | | [Alexandria](#alexandria) | Through Firecrawl Cloud after `firecrawl-local login` | ✅ | | [Interact](#interact), [Agent](#agent) and [Monitor](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/monitoring) | | ✅ | Scraping, crawling and mapping run on your machine. By default a single-page scrape that won't load there is fetched by Firecrawl Cloud instead and marked `"source": "firecrawl-cloud"` in the result. Those Cloud calls work without an account at a limited rate, and `firecrawl-local login` puts them on your Firecrawl account. Set `FIRECRAWL_CLOUD=off` to keep everything on your machine. --- ## Firecrawl Cloud Firecrawl Cloud runs everything Firecrawl Local does at scale, with no browser or machine of your own to look after. It also gives your AI agents access to far more knowledge than scraping alone, with search, Alexandria, Interact and Agent all through a single API. - **Works on the real web.** Covers 96% of the web, including JS-heavy pages and dynamic apps ([see benchmarks](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/the-worlds-best-web-data-api-v25)). - **Fast.** P95 latency of 3.4s across millions of pages, built for real-time AI agents and dynamic apps. - **LLM-ready output.** Clean markdown, structured JSON, screenshots and more, so your AI agents spend fewer tokens. [Firecrawl Keyless](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-keyless-launch) gives you 1,000 free credits a month with no API key or signup across MCP, the CLI and the API. For an API key, sign up at [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev) and try it in the [playground](https://firecrawl.dev/playground). ### Search Search the web and get full content from results. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") search_result = app.search("firecrawl", limit=5) ```
Node.js / cURL / CLI **Node.js** ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"}); app.search("firecrawl", { limit: 5 }) ``` **cURL** ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "query": "firecrawl", "limit": 5 }' ``` **CLI** ```bash firecrawl search "firecrawl" --limit 5 ```
```json [ { "url": "https://firecrawl.dev", "title": "Firecrawl", "markdown": "Turn websites into..." }, { "url": "https://docs.firecrawl.dev", "title": "Firecrawl Docs", "markdown": "# Getting Started..." } ] ``` ### Scrape Get LLM-ready context from any website as markdown, JSON, screenshots and more. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") result = app.scrape('firecrawl.dev') ```
Node.js / cURL / CLI **Node.js** ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY" }); app.scrape('firecrawl.dev') ``` **cURL** ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "url": "firecrawl.dev" }' ``` **CLI** ```bash firecrawl scrape https://firecrawl.dev firecrawl https://firecrawl.dev --only-main-content ```
``` # Firecrawl Firecrawl helps AI agents search, scrape, and interact with the web. ## Features - Search: Find information across the web - Scrape: Clean data from any page - Interact: Click, navigate, and operate pages - Agent: Autonomous data gathering ``` ### Interact Scrape a page, then interact with it using AI prompts or code. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") result = app.scrape("https://amazon.com") scrape_id = result.metadata.scrape_id app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Search for 'mechanical keyboard'") app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Click the first result") ```
Node.js / cURL / CLI **Node.js** ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"}); const result = await app.scrape("https://amazon.com"); await app.interact(result.metadata.scrapeId, { prompt: "Search for 'mechanical keyboard'" }); await app.interact(result.metadata.scrapeId, { prompt: "Click the first result" }); ``` **cURL** ```bash # 1. Scrape the page curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"url": "https://amazon.com"}' # 2. Interact with the page (use scrapeId from step 1) curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape/SCRAPE_ID/interact' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt": "Search for mechanical keyboard"}' ``` **CLI** ```bash firecrawl scrape https://amazon.com firecrawl interact exec --prompt "Search for 'mechanical keyboard'" firecrawl interact exec --prompt "Click the first result" ```
```json { "success": true, "output": "Keyboard available at $100", "liveViewUrl": "https://liveview.firecrawl.dev/..." } ``` ### Agent Describe what you need, and our AI agent searches, navigates and retrieves it with no URLs required. ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/agent' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "prompt": "Find the pricing plans for Notion" }' ``` ```json { "success": true, "data": { "result": "Notion offers the following pricing plans:\n\n1. Free - $0/month...\n2. Plus - $10/seat/month...\n3. Business - $18/seat/month...", "sources": ["https://www.notion.so/pricing"] } } ``` Pass a schema to get structured data back. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import List, Optional app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") class Founder(BaseModel): name: str = Field(description="Full name of the founder") role: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Role or position") class FoundersSchema(BaseModel): founders: List[Founder] = Field(description="List of founders") result = app.agent( prompt="Find the founders of Firecrawl", schema=FoundersSchema ) print(result.data) ``` The [Agent documentation](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/agent) covers starting URLs, effort levels and the `spark-2` model. ### Crawl Crawl an entire website and get content from all pages. ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/crawl' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "url": "https://docs.firecrawl.dev", "limit": 100, "scrapeOptions": { "formats": ["markdown"] } }' ``` It returns a job ID, and the [SDKs](#sdks) poll it for you until the crawl finishes. ```json { "success": true, "id": "123-456-789", "url": "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/crawl/123-456-789" } ``` ### Map Discover all URLs on a website instantly. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") result = app.map("https://firecrawl.dev", search="pricing") # Returns URLs ordered by relevance to "pricing" ``` ### Batch Scrape Scrape many URLs at once. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") job = app.batch_scrape([ "https://firecrawl.dev", "https://docs.firecrawl.dev", "https://firecrawl.dev/pricing" ], formats=["markdown"]) for doc in job.data: print(doc.metadata.source_url) ``` ### Alexandria [Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev) gives your AI agents 550+ data providers in one library (250M+ people, 75M+ companies, 41M+ research papers), plus specialized indexes and the live web, through one API, MCP or CLI. AI agents discover a tool alongside their web results, inspect its inputs and pricing, then run it to get structured data. Discovery is free, and running a tool uses the credits listed on it. Install it in your AI agent from [alexandria.firecrawl.dev](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev), or see the [Alexandria documentation](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alexandria) for CLI, MCP, SDK and API usage. Alexandria runs on Firecrawl Cloud, and Firecrawl Local can use it once you sign in with `firecrawl-local login`. ### Connect your AI agent The Firecrawl CLI gives your AI agent every Cloud tool with one command. It works with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code), [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google), [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and more, so restart your agent after installing. ```bash npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser ``` Any MCP client can connect with this config. ```json { "mcpServers": { "firecrawl-mcp": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"], "env": { "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "fc-YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } ``` An AI agent can sign up its user and get an API key by fetching the onboarding skill. ```bash curl -s https://firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md ``` See the [Skill and CLI documentation](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli) for every command, and [firecrawl-mcp-server](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server) for MCP. ### SDKs The SDKs cover every Firecrawl feature and poll async jobs for you. They work with Firecrawl Cloud, and with Firecrawl Local once you set the API URL to `http://localhost:3002`. #### Python ```bash pip install firecrawl ``` ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") # Scrape a single URL doc = app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev", formats=["markdown"]) print(doc.markdown) # Use the Agent for autonomous data gathering result = app.agent(prompt="Find the founders of Stripe") print(result.data) # Crawl a website (automatically waits for completion) docs = app.crawl("https://docs.firecrawl.dev", limit=50) for doc in docs.data: print(doc.metadata.source_url, doc.markdown[:100]) # Search the web results = app.search("best AI data tools 2024", limit=10) print(results) ``` #### Node.js ```bash npm install firecrawl ``` ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({ apiKey: 'fc-YOUR_API_KEY' }); // Scrape a single URL const doc = await app.scrape('https://firecrawl.dev', { formats: ['markdown'] }); console.log(doc.markdown); // Use the Agent for autonomous data gathering const result = await app.agent({ prompt: 'Find the founders of Stripe' }); console.log(result.data); // Crawl a website (automatically waits for completion) const docs = await app.crawl('https://docs.firecrawl.dev', { limit: 50 }); docs.data.forEach(doc => { console.log(doc.metadata.sourceURL, doc.markdown.substring(0, 100)); }); // Search the web const results = await app.search('best AI data tools 2024', { limit: 10 }); results.data.web.forEach(result => { console.log(`${result.title}: ${result.url}`); }); ``` #### More languages | Language | Install | Guide | |----------|---------|-------| | Go | `go get github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/apps/go-sdk` | [Go SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/go) | | Java | `com.firecrawl:firecrawl-java` from Maven Central | [Java SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/java) | | Rust | `cargo add firecrawl` | [Rust SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/rust) | | Ruby | `gem install firecrawl-sdk` | [Ruby SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/ruby) | | .NET | `dotnet add package firecrawl-sdk` | [.NET SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/dotnet) | | PHP | `composer require firecrawl/firecrawl-sdk` | [PHP SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/php) | | Elixir | `{:firecrawl, "~> 1.0"}` in `mix.exs` | [Elixir SDK](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/elixir) | ### Integrations **AI agents and tools** - [Firecrawl Skills Catalog](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills), installed with `npx skills add firecrawl/skills` - [Firecrawl CLI](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli) - [Firecrawl MCP](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server) The build skills for integrating Firecrawl into product code live in this repo under [`skills/`](./skills), and CI mirrors them into the catalog. To contribute a skill, send CLI skills (including the research and developer index skills) to [`firecrawl/cli`](https://github.com/firecrawl/cli), build and SDK skills to this repo's `skills/` folder, and workflow skills to [`firecrawl/firecrawl-workflows`](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-workflows). The catalog at [`firecrawl/skills`](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills) is read-only, so never open a PR against it directly. **Platforms** - [Lovable](https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/firecrawl) - [Zapier](https://zapier.com/apps/firecrawl/integrations) - [n8n](https://n8n.io/integrations/firecrawl/) [View all integrations →](https://www.firecrawl.dev/integrations) **Missing your favorite tool?** [Open an issue](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/issues) and let us know! ### Resources - [Documentation](https://docs.firecrawl.dev) - [API Reference](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/introduction) - [Playground](https://firecrawl.dev/playground) - [Changelog](https://firecrawl.dev/changelog) --- ## Self-hosting ![Open Source vs Cloud](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/img/open-source-cloud.png) [Firecrawl Local](#firecrawl-local) is the easiest way to run Firecrawl yourself. If you really want the full Firecrawl server with its own queues, workers and databases, all of it still lives in this repo and you can run it on your own infrastructure. If you'd rather not run anything yourself, [Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud) gives you every feature with no setup. The server runs with Docker Compose alongside Redis, PostgreSQL and a browser service, and the [self-hosting guide](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/contributing/self-host) takes you from checkout to your first scrape. Alexandria runs on Firecrawl Cloud, so the self-hosted server does not include it. --- ## Contributing We love contributions! # Google One 工具包（MuMu 模拟器 + Frida）

**`g1.30tb`已在大部分区域下架，可以先搞搞3个月打折的Ultra 5X**

通过 Frida 注入模拟器里的 Google One 进程，调用 Play BillingClient：
**扫描账号可用的全部订阅 offer（免费/付费）**，以及**拉起任意 SKU 的 Play 收银台**（只弹出，不自动订阅）。

---

## 文件清单

| 文件 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `ultra0_core.py` | 自包含核心（adb/frida-server/计费模块/注入模板，从原 ultra0.py 抽取） |
| `extract_core.py` | 生成器：从原版 ultra0.py 重新抽取 ultra0_core.py（仅维护时用） |
| `one_common.py` | 公共环境准备（选设备/root/frida-server/计费模块/Play 商店保活），所有脚本共用 |
| `launch_checkout.py` + `launch_checkout.js` | **拉起任意 SKU 收银台**（主力脚本） |
| `scan_all.py` | 全量扫描 70 个候选 SKU 的所有 offer（免费+付费+token），零风险 |
| `query_sku.py` | 只查指定几个 SKU，零风险 |
| `probe_env.py` | 环境诊断（frida 版本 / Java 桥 / Play 商店状态），出问题先跑它 |
| `scan_everything.py` + `scan_offers.js` | 穷举账号全部 SKU，输出带定价阶段的原始 JSON 并渲染清单 |
| `render_multi.py` | 合并多地区 JSON，生成 `SKU-清单.md` |
| `scan_result_*.json` | 各地区扫描原始数据（已脱敏：serial 已掩码、token 已置空） |
| `SKU-清单.md` | 多地区金额对照 + 人民币比价清单 |

> 整个文件夹**自包含、无外部依赖**：把 `google-one-tools` 拷到任何机器（装有
> Python3.9+ 和 frida 16.x）都能直接跑，不需要原版仓库里的脚本。

## 环境要求（缺一不可）

1. **本机 frida 必须 16.x**（推荐 16.7.19）：
   ```powershell
   py -m pip install frida==16.7.19
   ```
   > ⚠️ frida 17.x 在 MuMu（Android 12 / x86_64）上 Java 桥损坏（`Java is not defined`），
   > 所有功能静默失效。设备上的 frida-server 也必须同版本（脚本会自动下载匹配版）。
2. **自包含核心**：所有对原版 `ultra0.py` 的依赖已抽取进 `ultra0_core.py`，
   本文件夹可整体拷贝到别处使用；要更新抽取范围，改 `extract_core.py` 后重跑 `py extract_core.py`。
3. 模拟器已 root、已登录 Google 账号、装有 Google One 和 Play 商店。
4. 用 `py` 而不是 `python`（本机的 `python` 是商店占位符，跑不了）。

## 快速上手

```powershell
cd C:\path\to\google-one-tools

# 0. 环境自检（第一次先跑这个）
py probe_env.py

# 1. 扫描当前账号的全部 offer（免费+付费，不下单）
py scan_all.py                       # 自动选第一台模拟器
py scan_all.py 127.0.0.1:16384       # 多开时指定实例

# 2. 只查某几个 SKU
py query_sku.py g1.30tb g1.20tb

# 3. 拉起收银台（弹出后人工确认，脚本不点订阅）
py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.20tb                    # 自动选设备
py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.30tb 127.0.0.1:16384    # 指定实例
```

## SKU 对照表

| 档位 | SKU | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 30 GB / 100GB / 200GB | `g1.30gb` / `g1.100gb` / `g1.200gb` | 基础存储 |
| 2TB / 5TB / 10TB / 20TB / 30TB | `g1.2tb` / `g1.5tb` / `g1.10tb` / `g1.20tb` / `g1.30tb` | 基础存储 |
| 年付版 | 上面任一 + `.annual`（如 `g1.2tb.annual`） | 部分档无年付 |
| AI Plus (400GB) | `g1.play.helium` | 常有 12/6/3/1 月免费试用 |
| AI Pro (5TB) | `g1.2tb.ai.subs_variant` | 常有 12+6+6+6 月免费试用 |
| Ultra 20TB | `g1.play.20tb` | 试用看账号资格 |
| Ultra AI Pro (30TB) | `g1.play.ai.pro` / `g1.30tb` | 多数号无试用 |
| 2TB 首三月折扣 | `g1.2tb.3months_ip_85p.acq` | introprice，非免费 |

> 免费试用档基本只挂在**带 `play` 前缀**或 **`subs_variant`** 的 SKU 上；
> 带 `.eft` 后缀的是试用专用 SKU。以 `scan_all.py` 的实际返回为准。

## 多模拟器实例

- `pick_device` 默认选 adb 列表第一台。**多开时必须指定**：位置参数或环境变量 `SERIAL`：
  ```powershell
  py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.20tb 127.0.0.1:16384
  $env:SERIAL="127.0.0.1:16384"; py scan_all.py
  ```
  （`16384` 只是 MuMu 12 的默认 ADB 端口；多开实例的实际端口以 `adb devices` 为准。）
- frida 连接按 serial 精确匹配，不会串台。

## VPN 共存（本工具包刻意支持）

- **不调用** `ultra0.ensure_network()`：不清设备代理、不杀 Clash/v2rayNG。
- 注入走 adb 通道（127.0.0.1:xxxxx），与模拟器内 VPN 互不影响。
- 建议 VPN 用**分应用模式**，排除这三个包让结算直连：
  `com.android.vending`、`com.google.android.gms`、`com.google.android.apps.subscriptions.red`
  （或 TUN 模式把 DNS 从 fake-ip 改 redir-host，否则 Play 结算可能连不上。）

## 故障排查（按命中频率排序）

| 症状 | 原因 | 解法 |
|---|---|---|
| 收银台不弹出、Play 商店像是「死了」；logcat 有 `InAppBillingService ... crashed service` / `Monetization gRPC call timeout` / `:recovery_mode failed to attach` | **VPN（如 Surfshark）劫持了 Play 的网络**，结算服务崩溃重启 | ① Surfshark → 设置 → VPN 设置 → 分应用代理(Split tunneling) → 排除 `Google Play 商店`、`Google Play 服务`、`Google One`；② 或跑收银台前先断开 VPN |
| 未收到 `launched` 事件 | Play 商店没在跑（脚本会自动拉，但可能拉不起来） | 跑 `py probe_env.py` 看 vending 状态 |
| Play 商店反复 `failed to attach` / `start timeout` | Play 商店假死（连拉多次收银台后常见） | **重启模拟器**：`adb -s <serial> reboot`，10 秒开机不亏 |
| 收银台弹出瞬间 Play 商店崩（ScionFrontendAp SIGABRT） | MuMu 镜像上 Play 商店老版本 bug | 模拟器里升级 Play 商店，或清其数据 |
| Java 桥 `hasJava:false` | 本机或设备 frida 是 17.x | `py -m pip install frida==16.7.19`，删设备 `/data/local/tmp/frida-server` 重跑 |
| 重启模拟器后脚本报「没有 root」 | adb root 后 adbd 瞬断 | 本工具包的 `ensure_root_retry` 已自动重试；旧脚本需手动 `adb -s <serial> root` |
| 查询空 offer | frida 坏了（Java 桥死）或 SKU 在该账号地区不存在 | 先 `probe_env.py`；再看 SKU 是否在该地区上架 |

## 重要注意

- `launchBillingFlow` 返回 code=0 **即可能消耗该账号的试用资格**，即使你最后没点订阅——别对同一个号反复拉免费档。
- 收银台弹出不点订阅不会扣费；点了订阅按显示价格扣费。
- 免费试用结束会自动续费，记得提前取消。

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,861 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical


Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: record, replay and the front door today; unit ports come next.

Record
record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws. 		Port
bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust. 		Check
diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes. 		Lift
When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on [napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). ## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | Kotlin | Gradle module of top-level functions and `@JvmStatic` methods | the Java bridge: typed JNI in Java wrapper classes calling the compiled Kotlin statics | a generated reflection driver, with the Kotlin sources compiled by `kotlinc` | | PHP | folder of functions and `public static` methods | coming next: PHP FFI over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | C# | folder of `public static` methods | coming next: P/Invoke over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); a Gradle module with `.kt` sources and no `.java` sources is Kotlin, mixed modules stay Java. `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java, Kotlin and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. For Android, `rust-anything build --profile android` builds the same JNI library with the NDK for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a` and `x86_64` (or the `--abi` values you pass) and installs it into `/jniLibs//`; `--api` sets the API level (minimum 26, which the generated Java runtime needs). It finds the NDK from `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`/`ANDROID_NDK_ROOT` or the SDK, needs the Rust targets (`rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi x86_64-linux-android`), links 64-bit libraries with 16 KB page alignment, and checks that every JNI entry point is exported. Gradle looks in `src/main/jniLibs` by default, so pass `--jni-libs app/src/main/jniLibs` or add `/jniLibs` to `sourceSets.main.jniLibs.srcDirs`. `rust-anything record --profile android` runs the original Kotlin unit under ART on a connected device (adb), dexes the generated driver with `d8` from the SDK's build-tools, and pulls the results back as the same `cases.jsonl`; `diff --profile android` replays them against the `.so` built for the device's ABI. Both need `adb`, a device, `kotlinc`, an SDK with build-tools and a platform, and `--device ` when more than one device is connected. The profile covers logic units: Activity/Compose/XML UI, lifecycle and SDK-only classes stay in Kotlin, and each call crosses JNI, so prefer the generated batch wrappers for hot loops. On a host, `record` and `diff` keep using the desktop JVM. For PHP, `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. Porting its units into Rust through PHP's FFI is the next step ([issue #2](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/2)). C# works the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door; porting units through P/Invoke comes next. ## Learn more - [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): the loop, what `bridge` and `analyze` decide, hot paths, what it can't catch, what a real port takes, and keeping up with the original (`map`) - [Ship a port as a package](docs/packaging.md): maturin wheels and napi-rs per-platform npm packages, with the CI that builds them - [Port a whole app](docs/whole-apps.md): servers, CLIs and libraries, from the front door to `app lift` - [Examples and case studies](docs/examples.md): x18n, and real code in six languages - [Real-world ports](docs/real-world.md): json-server, Fuse.js, vercel/ms, with benchmarks - [Install, update and develop](docs/install.md): every install method, Windows, and building from source - [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Status](docs/STATUS.md) · [MCP tools](docs/tools.md) ## Sponsors
